AI/context-engineers.title: context engineers
AI/context-engineers.content:
Context Engineers: The System Orchestrators of Agentic AI



                  
                  KEY
                  
                

A Context Engineer is a software architect who designs the external cognitive environment—instructions, workspace memory, tool protocols, and guardrails—surrounding an AI model. Rather than writing raw procedural code, context engineers structure deterministic Markdown files to orchestrate autonomous Large Language Models.


What is a Context Engineer?
A Context Engineer is an agentic systems designer who constructs the operational environment that constrains and directs AI models. As foundation models reach performance equilibrium, the primary bottleneck in software engineering is no longer raw model intelligence—it is the quality, structure, and precision of the local context provided to the model.

“Context accounts for 90% of your AI capabilities and intelligence; the remaining 10% comes from the model you choose to place in your harness.”


The 6 Types of AI Context
In an Agentic Harness, a context engineer structures six distinct layers of information:








































Context LayerPrimary FunctionPractical Implementation in Markdown1. InstructionsDefining core roles, goals, and execution personaSystem prompts and CONTEXT.md high-level goals2. KnowledgeConnecting domain-specific data and schemasArchitectural diagrams, design tokens, and API docs3. MemoryManaging session state and long-term project historySession transcript logs and local .md project state4. ExamplesProviding few-shot behavioral demonstrationsGold-standard code snippets and testing patterns5. ToolsEquipping the agent with executable capabilitiesModel Context Protocol (MCP) servers and shell scripts6. GuardrailsEnforcing non-negotiable boundaries and rules.agents/rules.md and automated build verifications

Prompt Engineering vs. Context Engineering



































DimensionPrompt EngineeringContext EngineeringScopeSingle conversational query or prompt stringEntire workspace filesystem and tool environmentPersistenceEphemeral (resets every session)Deterministic (persists in local Markdown files)Execution MediumCloud chat interfacesLocal IDEs (Google Antigravity, Cursor) & MCP serversPrimary SkillNatural language phrasing & trickeryInformation architecture, schema design, and rule scopingScalabilityLow (manual re-prompting required)High (automated workspace indexing)
You can start learning context engineering for free by organizing your digital assets and documentation in Obsidian.

❓ Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
Why is Context Engineering replacing Prompt Engineering?
Because Large Language Models are stateless engines. Crafting clever one-off prompts cannot scale complex software systems. Context engineering creates persistent, version-controlled workspace rules and tool registries that ground the AI automatically on every invocation.
How do I get started as a Context Engineer?
Start by creating a single CONTEXT.md file in your project repository. Define your tech stack, project goals, non-negotiable boundaries, and key file paths. Point your AI IDE (such as Google Antigravity) to this file before requesting code generation.

Geopolitic/Amicus.title: Amicus
Geopolitic/Amicus.content:
KEY
                  
                

Public political figures rarely originate legislation in isolation; national strategy is overwhelmingly engineered by unelected networks of lobbyists, administrative rulemakers, and Amici Curiae legal foundations who supply pre-drafted policy frameworks.


Who Really Writes the Laws?
When we watch the news, we are taught to believe that elected officials—presidents, prime ministers, and legislators—are the sole architects of law and public policy.
In reality, elected figures are often the public faces for complex policy projects. Behind the podiums, the vast majority of bills, regulations, and executive orders are drafted, sponsored, and driven by unseen actors: policy advisors, corporate lobbyists, bureaucratic agencies, and legal advocacy groups (the Amici Curiae or “friends of the court”).


                  
                  The Frontman Illusion 
                  
                

Most citizens believe public figures originate national strategy. In practice, politicians operate with structural sponsors—networks of lobbyists, career bureaucrats, and legal think tanks who supply the pre-written legislation, legislative briefs, and regulatory frameworks ready for signature.
ICE Police forces aren’t Trump’s idea



The 3 Layers of Unseen Influence
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  LAYER 1: SPONSORS & LOBBYISTS (Financial & Special Interest Agendas) |
|  Draft model bills, fund campaigns, and shape legislative priorities. |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                   |
                                   v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  LAYER 2: BUREAUCRATIC AGENCIES & LEGAL ADVOCATES (Amici Curiae)     |
|  Write the detailed regulatory fine print and judicial legal briefs.  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                   |
                                   v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  LAYER 3: ELECTED PUBLIC FIGURES (The Frontmen)                       |
|  Sign documents, hold press conferences, and absorb public reactions. |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
1. Special Interest Sponsors & Model Legislation
Lobbyists and donor groups do not merely persuade lawmakers; they write complete laws. Organizations compile pre-drafted “model bills” that politicians introduce verbatim into legislative assemblies.
2. Administrative Agencies & Regulatory Rulemaking
Congress or Parliament passes broad laws, but the actual rules governing energy, finance, healthcare, and digital trade are written by non-elected agency officials through public administrative law and executive orders.
3. Legal Advocacy Groups (Amici Curiae)
In the judicial system, Amici Curiae (“friends of the court”) file legal briefs that shape high court decisions. Non-elected legal foundations supply the arguments, precedent interpretations, and draft opinions that judges incorporate directly into binding legal rulings.



                  
                  How Orders Become Law Behind Closed Doors 
                  
                

Rather than starting as a public debate, major policy directives often originate from internal advisory panels and special interest directives. By the time a bill reaches a public vote, its core mechanics have already been negotiated and locked in by non-elected architects.



Key Takeaway for Citizens
Understanding who really drives political decisions breaks the illusion of political theater.
To track real power, look beyond the speeches of public figures and examine:

Who drafted the bill’s specific clauses
Which special interest groups funded the underlying policy research
Which non-elected agency officials hold permanent regulatory authority

By following the sponsors rather than the spokespeople, you gain a clear, unvarnished view of how governance actually functions.

Geopolitic/Haiti-and-Administrative-Inva.title: Haïti & Administrative invasions
Geopolitic/Haiti-and-Administrative-Inva.content:
Haïti & Administrative Invasions (1915 – Present)
Since the early 20th century, Haiti has experienced a continuous sequence of external administrative interventions, financial takeovers, intelligence operations, and foreign diplomatic mandates.
While public narrative often attributes Haiti’s ongoing instability solely to internal failure, historical research demonstrates a structural pattern of administrative engineering—where foreign banking entities, foreign intelligence agencies, multilateral missions, and political elites have repeatedly robbed Haitian national sovereignty.



                  
                  Administrative Engineering 
                  
                

The substitution of a country self-governance with external control, international advisory boards, and proxy political decision makers. Rather than traditional colonization, administrative invasion operates through banking debt control, constitutional manipulation, paramilitary intelligence leverage, and diplomatic influence.



1. Wall Street & The 1914 Banking Takeover
The financial surrender of Haiti to US banking preceded military intervention:

The BNRH Stake Acquisition (1910): Under the guidance of National City Bank of New York executive Roger L. Farnham, a syndicate of American banks acquired a controlling interest in the Banque Nationale de la République d’Haïti (BNRH). The bank served as Haiti’s treasury, collecting customs duties and issuing currency.
The 500,000 Gold Reserve Seizure (December 17, 1914)**: Under instructions from the US State Department and National City Bank, US Marines landed in Port-au-Prince, entered the BNRH vaults, and confiscated **500,000 in Haitian gold reserves. The gold was loaded onto the gunboat USS Machias and transported to National City Bank vaults in New York to guarantee debt servicing to American creditors.
Financial Receivership: The gold seizure effectively paralyzed the Haitian state’s monetary sovereignty, creating a liquidity crisis that served as the immediate justification for military invasion seven months later.


2. The US Military Occupation & The 1918 Constitution (1915–1934)
On July 28, 1915, following the assassination of President Vilbrun Guillaume Sam, US Marines landed in Port-au-Prince, initiating a 19-year military occupation:

Customs Control & Revenue Diversion: US officials seized control of all customs houses, which generated over 80% of Haitian state revenue. Funds were prioritized to pay off American and French bondholders before any allocation to domestic public services or education.
The 1918 Constitution Rewrite: The occupation authority dissolved the Haitian National Assembly when it refused to pass a new constitution. The 1918 Constitution—drafted with direct involvement from Franklin D. Roosevelt (then Assistant Secretary of the Navy)—repealed Article 5 of the 1804 Constitution, which had banned foreign land ownership since independence.
The Corvée System & Caco Uprising: The military administration re-enacted the corvée—an 1864 law forcing Haitian peasants into unpaid labor to build military roads. This sparked the Caco Uprising, led by commander Charlemagne Péralte. Over 15,000 Haitians were killed during the counter-insurgency before Péralte was betrayed, executed in 1919, and photographed pinned to a door as a warning.
Creation of the Gendarmerie: The occupation established the Gendarmerie d’Haïti (later the Forces Armées d’Haïti / FAd’H), creating a militarized internal police force designed to maintain domestic order rather than defend national borders against foreign threat.

2.1 The Second Caco War (1918–1920) & The Brutal Event of May 18–19, 1920
The armed resistance against the US occupation reached its peak during the Second Caco War, led by supreme commanders Charlemagne Péralte and Benoît Batraville:

The Caco Resistance: Outraged by the re-imposition of forced labor (corvée) and foreign land appropriations under the 1918 Constitution, over 40,000 Haitian peasants joined or supported the Caco guerrilla forces against the US Marine Corps and the Gendarmerie d’Haïti.
Péralte’s Crucifixion & Batraville’s Command: Following the October 31, 1919 betrayal and assassination of Charlemagne Péralte (whose corpse was photographed tied to a door to resemble a crucifixion and distributed across Haiti as counter-insurgency propaganda), Benoît Batraville assumed supreme command of the Caco forces, continuing anti-occupation operations in the Central Plateau and Artibonite regions.
The Brutal Event of May 18–19, 1920: On May 18–19, 1920, US Marine Captain Hermann H. Hanneken and Marine patrols ambushed Batraville’s encampment near Mirebalais. Batraville was shot and killed on May 18, 1920. US Marine forces took his body, photographed it, and publicly displayed it in Mirebalais before burying it in an unmarked grave to break the psychological spirit of Haitian national resistance.
The Tragic Historical Paradox of May 18: A profound historical irony is that May 18 is celebrated nationwide in Haiti as Haitian Flag Day (Fête du Drapeau—commemorating the creation of the blue-and-red flag by Jean-Jacques Dessalines and Catherine Flon at Arcahaie in 1803). On May 18, 1920, while the occupied nation observed its national flag holiday, US Marine occupation forces executed and publicly desecrated the body of the last supreme commander of active anti-occupation resistance, effectively ending the Second Caco War while many citizens were unaware of the military execution taking place in Mirebalais on that exact date.


3. Cold War Dictatorship & Intelligence Alignment (1957–1986)
During the Cold War, foreign policy toward Haiti prioritized anti-communist alignment in the Caribbean over democratic governance:

The Duvalier Regimes: François “Papa Doc” Duvalier (1957–1971) and his son Jean-Claude “Baby Doc” Duvalier (1971–1986) built an authoritarian dictatorship sustained by the Tonton Macoutes (Volontaires de la Sécurité Nationale).
Geopolitical Leverage: Situated less than 60 miles from Fidel Castro’s Cuba, the Duvalier regime leveraged its anti-communist stance to secure millions of dollars in US military and economic assistance despite widespread extrajudicial killings and repression.
Economic Siphoning: Millions in foreign aid funds were siphoned into personal offshore accounts while domestic agricultural production collapsed under structural adjustment mandates, initiating rural-to-urban mass migration into Port-au-Prince slums.


4. The 1991 Coup, FRAPH, & Intelligence Assets (1991–1994)
In December 1990, Jean-Bertrand Aristide won Haiti’s first democratic election with 67% of the vote. Eight months into his presidency, he was overthrown in a bloody military coup on September 30, 1991:

The Military Junta: Led by General Raoul Cédras and Chief of Police Michel François, the junta executed thousands of Aristide supporters.
FRAPH & Emmanuel Constant: The Front pour l’Avancement et le Progrès d’Haïti (FRAPH), a death squad paramilitary network, was formed under Emmanuel “Toto” Constant. Official US government records later confirmed that Constant was a paid informant for the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) throughout the junta period.
Operation Uphold Democracy (1994): Under intense refugee pressure, 20,000 US troops landed in Haiti in September 1994 to restore Aristide. However, restoration was conditioned on implementing strict neoliberal economic reforms (tariff reductions on foreign rice) and the complete disbandment of the Haitian Armed Forces (FAd’H).


5. The 2004 Bicentennial Ouster & The Ottawa Initiative
As Haiti prepared to celebrate the 200th anniversary of its 1804 independence, international political pressure intensified:

The Bicentennial Restitution Demand (2003): President Aristide formally demanded that France reimburse Haiti the 1825 Independence Indemnity (150 million gold francs extorted under threat of war), calculated at $21.7 billion USD in modern valuation.
The Ottawa Initiative on Haiti (January 2003): High-level officials from Canada, the United States, France, and the OAS met in Ottawa, Canada. Reports published by journalist Michel Vastel revealed discussions regarding the removal of Aristide and the potential implementation of a UN trusteeship over Haiti.
The 2004 Rebellion & Exile: In February 2004, an armed insurgency composed of former FAd’H soldiers and FRAPH paramilitary leaders (Guy Philippe, Jodel Chamblain) launched an attack from the Dominican border. On February 29, 2004, US diplomats and security personnel escorted Aristide onto an unmarked American aircraft, flying him into exile in the Central African Republic. Aristide described the event as a “modern-day kidnapping.”


6. Multilateral Control: MINUSTAH & The “NGO State” (2004–2017)
Following the 2004 ouster, formal administration of Haiti was transferred to international multilateral organizations:

MINUSTAH Occupation (2004–2017): The United Nations Stabilization Mission in Haiti deployed thousands of foreign military troops and police.
The 2010 Cholera Outbreak: In October 2010, UN peacekeepers stationed at the Mirebalais base discharged untreated sewage containing Vibrio cholerae into the Meille River, a tributary of the Artibonite. The resulting epidemic killed over 10,000 Haitians and infected more than 800,000. The UN denied responsibility for six years before issuing a partial acknowledgment in 2016.

Grounding AI in local file context eliminates architectural drift, token waste, and cognitive fatigue.


This guide was designed for Google Antigravity users.


                  
                  Freedom of Context: Start Simple 
                  
                

You do not need to enforce a rigid multi-directory harness when starting out. As a pragmatic programmer, your harness will often consist of a single CONTEXT.md file containing your project instructions, boundaries, and stack rules. The multi-layer framework (rules, skills, MCP APIs, subagents) is simply a modular architecture that grows organically as your project scales.



What is an Agentic Harness?
An Agentic Harness is the deterministic software scaffolding that surrounds a non-deterministic Large Language Model. Rather than letting an AI model guess your project conventions from a blank prompt, the harness supplies structured workspace memory, tools, and execution boundaries.

“Context accounts for 90% of an autonomous agent’s real-world capability; the remaining 10% comes from the underlying foundation model.”

An Agentic Harness consists of four foundational layers:

System Instructions & Boundaries: Establishing persona, conventions, and non-negotiable constraints.
Persistent Workspace Memory: Retaining project architecture via local Markdown (CONTEXT.md).
Tool Registries (MCP APIs): Connecting AI to local filesystems, terminal shells, and external APIs via the Model Context Protocol.
Empirical Verification Loops: Automatically running build commands and tests after code modifications to catch errors before deployment.


Why does AI need structured context?
Without structured local context, AI models operate as blank slates with zero memory of your codebase conventions, API schemas, or architectural constraints. Relying solely on raw prompts leads to three critical failure modes:

Hallucination & Architectural Drift: The model imports non-existent libraries, fabricates parameter types, and violates project patterns.
Cognitive Fatigue: The developer wastes hours re-explaining folder hierarchies and tech stack rules in every prompt.
Broken Vibe Coding: Unconstrained code generation creates fragile, untracked modifications that fail silently in production.



                  
                  The Context Window Principle 
                  
                

Grounding an AI in local project context bridges the gap between raw LLM capabilities and your exact project reality. By organizing context into local Markdown files, you index memory deterministically, eliminating noise and transforming the AI into a high-precision execution partner.

What is YAML Frontmatter?
YAML (YAML Ain’t Markup Language) frontmatter is a human- and machine-readable metadata block placed at the beginning of a Markdown note between triple dashes (---).
It provides three foundational advantages:

The Most Sophisticated Manual Data Organization: Transforms flat text files into queryable relational databases without complex software.
The Most Token-Efficient AI Context Layer: Injects structured categorical parameters into Large Language Models using minimal token overhead.
Universal Interoperability: Readable by humans, Obsidian Dataview, static site generators (Quartz), and local AI agent harnesses alike.

All you need to do is type --- at the very top of your note to initialize your frontmatter properties.

The Sovereign Frontmatter Schema
---
# Identity & Taxonomy
title: "The Exact Title"
publish: false             # Set to true to make the page public (private by default)
created: YYYY-MM-DD        # History (creation date)
modified: YYYY-MM-DD       # Freshness (last modified date)
author: Jason              # The Human Source (Default)
description: ""            # A 150-char hook designed for Google Click-Through Rate & AI Overviews
tags: []                   # Topics (bracketed: [tag1, tag2])
aliases: []                # Alternate Title, Misspelling, Voice Search Phrase
cssclasses: []             # Custom CSS styling classes
cover: ""                  # Relative path to image (Required for Master Notes)
---
You can customize your YAML schema to include any domain-specific properties you need (e.g., status: in-progress, type: case-study, links: []).
